subject: Hosted API privacy Q&A — public-facing plain-language copy
messages:
From: Olivia Mendez <olivia.mendez@acme-client.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: plain-language privacy Q&A for hosted API portal

Hi Evelyn / team,

Hope you’re well. As we prepare our procurement packet for the July security review, the Acme privacy team asked for a short, public-facing Q&A that explains: how Redwood handles customer data for the Hosted API (including examples of subprocessors and how data transfers are addressed), what the DPA covers, and a one-paragraph plain-language summary we can include in our vendor list.

High level asks:
- A 3–4 question Q&A that can be posted on your privacy portal and linked from our procurement docs.
- A brief sentence about region controls (we need to confirm whether data can be pinned to a region).
- A current list of subprocessors (or a link) and the type of processing they do.

We don’t need the full DPA redline yet — just the public copy and a short blurb. Is that something you can share this week?

Thanks,
Olivia
Privacy & Compliance, Acme Corp

--
Acme Corp (privacy@acme-client.com)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Mendez <olivia.mendez@acme-client.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: plain-language privacy Q&A for hosted API portal

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask. We can definitely produce a short public Q&A and a one-paragraph summary for your vendor pack.

Plan: I’ll coordinate an internal draft with Legal and Product, then send a short doc for your review. Two quick clarifying Qs before we start:
1) Do you want the subprocessors listed by name on the public page, or would a link to a maintained subprocessor map suffice?
2) Is it important that the Q&A explicitly mention the DPA and point to a downloadable PDF, or should it remain high level with a link to contact sales for full DPA access?

I’ll target a first draft by Thursday EOD.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Olivia Mendez <olivia.mendez@acme-client.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 15:30:00 -0400
Subject: Draft: Public-facing Q&A snippets (legal)

Evelyn / Olivia / team,

Attached is a short draft I put together for the portal (privacy_portal_qna_v1.docx). I focused on plain language and avoided legalese; the idea is to make the content consumable by procurement reviewers and engineers alike. Key points included:
- What data we process and why (request/response tokens; no persistent customer inference data unless configured)
- DPA coverage and how to request a copy
- Subprocessor overview + link to maintained map
- Data transfer approach and safeguards (SCCs + encryption in transit & at rest)

A couple of legal notes for the internal team:
- We should avoid committing to per-request deletion guarantees on the public page; keep deletion/retention policies in the DPA and docs.
- For subprocessors, the public page can reference our maintained list; detailed contracts should be shared under NDA if an external legal asks.

Olivia — if this looks like the right tone, we can finalize for your procurement packet.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: privacy_portal_qna_v1.docx (word doc with Q&A snippets)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Mendez <olivia.mendez@acme-client.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Public-facing Q&A snippets (legal)

Thanks Kim — great baseline. A few product/UX suggestions for the portal copy so it reads well on the Hosted API console page: 

- Make the Q titles shorter (e.g., "What data does Redwood process?") and use a one-line answer plus a "Learn more" link.
- Move technical examples (tokens, logs) to a collapsible section so the page stays short for non-technical reviewers.
- For region language: say "Customers can request data processing to be routed to a specific region; options depend on plan and capacity" — avoids a hard guarantee while being clear.

I added inline edits to Kim's doc and dropped a Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG_privacy_portal (see file "privacy_portal_qna_v1_laura_edits.docx").

Happy to help with the final copy and console placement mock.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Console

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Mendez <olivia.mendez@acme-client.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Public-facing Q&A snippets (legal)

Quick security/infra clarification for the public copy:

- Data transfers: we should be explicit that when traffic leaves a customer-specified region for inference (e.g., queued or routed for capacity), it is protected by contractual transfers (Standard Contractual Clauses) and that we encrypt in transit and at rest.
- Subprocessors: attaching an internal CSV with the current set (subprocessor_summary_20260802.csv). On the public page we should state "A maintained list of subprocessors is available and updated regularly" with a link; don't publish the CSV on the public site.

Also flagging one sentence for Legal: "Redwood does not use customer prompts or generated outputs to train models unless customers opt in via a dedicated data-sharing agreement." We should confirm whether we want that level of specificity publicly.

Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_summary_20260802.csv

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Mendez <olivia.mendez@acme-client.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Final: Public-facing Q&A + one-paragraph summary for Acme procurement

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the request and your patience while we pulled internal stakeholders together. Attached is a short packet that includes:

1) A 3-question public Q&A intended for the privacy portal (file: privacy_portal_qna_v1.docx) — concise answers with a "Learn more" link to the full DPA.
2) A one-paragraph plain-language vendor blurb you can paste into your procurement vendor list that confirms the DPA covers Hosted API processing and points customers to the subprocessor map.
3) Internal notes for Acme (not for the public page) that clarify region routing language and confirmation that model training does not occur with customer data unless explicitly opted in.

Links & attachments:
- Portal draft (attached): privacy_portal_qna_v1.docx
- Current subprocessor summary (attached, internal): subprocessor_summary_20260802.csv
- Drive folder with editable copies: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG_privacy_portal

Next steps for us: if the attached Q&A looks good, let us know if you want us to provide a short HTML snippet for your internal portal or if you prefer a PDF. If your legal team needs the full DPA, I can connect you to our contracts team and create a secure link.

Would you like a brief call to walk through the packet Thursday morning PST?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192
